narration: Your brain is doing this to you right now.
You probably believe this: MONEY BUYS HAPPINESS DIRECTLY. But that's not the full story.

Buying TIME, outsourcing chores you hate, reliably raises life satisfaction more than buying stuff. Here's what's happening: Feeling 'time-poor' is one of the strongest negative predictors of well-being. Stuff doesn't fix it; minutes do.
Whillans and colleagues 2017, PNAS: people who spent money on time-saving services reported greater life satisfaction, replicated across countries.
Before your next impulse buy, ask: could this money buy me back 3 hours instead? Hours win. That's your Mindforge move for today. Follow for tomorrow's.
